cells.tense: You are here, and what you started is standing up on its own in front of you.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Pick the one direction that matters most for what you are growing, and hold to it for a week, even when the old surveying pulls you back.
cells.core:
Something that began as bare possibility has grown into a thing you can stand beside. It has weight now because it is real, and that weight is not a problem to solve. You know how to tend what is still forming; you are good at leaving room and not forcing. That part is working.

The invitation is to name where this goes. Decide the heading, then stop reviewing every other branch. The caring underneath doesn't change — it simply gets a bearing.

Once a thing is this far along, it will take your direction without breaking. Deciding the heading is not a course correction. It is the next thing care does.
cells.sheetLine: What you grew can now take a direction from you.
cells.verb: carrying what possibility became until it stands finished on its own
cells.place: in the patch where something young is still making its way up

cells.tense: You will have it finished in your head before it has finished growing in the ground.
cells.act: see the thing as if for the first time
cells.ask: Once this week, look at what you are growing with no plan in your head, and take it in as it is today.
cells.core:
You can already see how this turns out, the whole shape of what it should become, and you are pulling the thing toward that picture before it has had a season. The correcting starts before the growth does. Something still forming that gets read for its harvest too early gets handled like produce, and whoever is inside it can feel the hurry from someone who already knows how they end up.

What is thin here is seeing what is actually there today. Not the plan, not the version that should exist. The thing as it is this morning, with its own pace and its own surprises still in it.

Look at what you are growing with your hands still. Let it be new for a minute. The direction you want will still be there, and it will be truer from ground level.
cells.sheetLine: You see the harvest before the seedling has its season.

cells.tense: You passed the point where this was possible for you, and the door is behind you.
cells.act: sit somewhere new with nothing in your hands and let whatever comes, come
cells.ask: Sit somewhere you don't usually sit, hands empty, and stay ten minutes with whatever shows up.
cells.core:
Something that once could have grown under your care has gone quiet. You are still near it, but the work has stopped, and your attention has drifted from what a seed would need. It is not that you forgot how. The spot you were facing is behind you now, and you have not turned around to where you actually are.

No effort will start this. Pushing harder into the vacant spot just makes the vacancy louder. What opens a door like this is receiving something modest, on its terms, with no verdict waiting after.

Sit somewhere new with your hands empty. Stay ten minutes and don't name what arrives. Once something plain has actually fed you, the care you carry will find where to go.
cells.sheetLine: The door is behind you. You're still at it.
cells.verb: carrying what possibility became until it stands finished on its own
cells.place: in the patch where something young is still making its way up

cells.tense: A direction is being carried here and the one carrying it hasn't signed for it.
cells.act: let the vision be shared with one other
cells.ask: Put what you are growing toward into your own words for one person who will hear it, and let their response stand.
cells.core:
You saw something worth growing — a direction for something you care about — and you acted on it without ever calling it yours. Said out loud, it comes through as what the group is doing, or what should happen. Ask you, and it was nobody's idea in particular. But you have been keeping it going. That work has been yours for a while, and the direction behind it has only ever been carried by you.

What gets lost this way is not the work. It is the sharing. A vision held alone can still flow; an unclaimed one gets carried privately, and something that wants two streams stays one.

The small next thing is to let it out. What you are growing toward, said as yours, to somebody who will hear it.
cells.sheetLine: The vision is yours. You haven't said so.

The reader could reasonably say the real situation is that nothing ever got started rather than something finished — the Too Little cell answers that directly, since the seed that never sprouted is what a door already behind you means. The ask survives being wrong: putting a wanted thing in place of the old one is small, private, and teaches the person something about where their hours actually go even if the read is off. The sentence that served me more than them was 'you already decided this without noticing' in the Unacknowledged core — it put a whole history in their mouth, so I narrowed it to the carrying and the sharing. Every ask here is the partner's own act, done small, and the four open on different verbs.
